court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
case_name: 63, Moons Technologies Limited vs Union Of India & 10 Others

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Moons Technologies Limited (formerly Financial Technologies (India) Ltd. & Ors.)

facts_of_case: Petitioners are Moons Technologies Limited, formerly known as Financial Technologies (India) Ltd., and others. Respondents are the Union of India and others. The petitioners claim that the impugned order is ultra vires Section 396 of the Companies Act.

legal_principles.principle: The mechanism of paired contracts adopted at the NSEL exchange between 2009 and until the collapse of operations in 2013 was very similar to the abuse referred to in Statement of Objects and Reasons to the Amendment Act.
legal_principles.held: By resort to such a modus operandi, the transactions at the NSEL Exchange no longer remained any genuine spot delivery transactions or ready delivery transactions or even forward transactions of one day's duration.

legal_principles.principle: Transactions that assume the character of pure and simple financing transactions are not genuine spot delivery or ready delivery transactions.
legal_principles.held: These paired contracts were obviously in breach of the conditions of the exemption notification and consequently the FCRA itself.
